title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is insider misuse of a deployed system rather than a failure of the system's own logic. A license plate reader network built to support police investigations was queried repeatedly by the person with authorised access to it, and the queries were pointed at two private individuals over a period of months. The technology performed as designed. The control that failed was the one governing who may direct it and at whom.

The misuse sat at the point of access, where a single authorised user can run lookups without a second party involved. Catching it would have required the query record to be reviewed against a stated investigative purpose, so that repeated checks on the same two people with no case attached would surface as an anomaly. Nothing in the account indicates that such a review existed or that it flagged the pattern before it was reported.

The account rests on a Kansas certification order and on reporting, and the order is the source for the admission that jealousy affected his actions. The summary does not establish a criminal conviction, and the reported counts of the checks differ between the headline and the order.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: From June to October 2023, Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard reportedly used Flock Safety license plate readers 228 times to check where his former girlfriend and her new boyfriend were, according to a Kansas certification order. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and later admitted that jealousy affected his actions. Nygaard resigned in October 2023 and later lost his police certification.
